original_question: Determine the exact asymptotic growth of D(n), where D(n) is the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set in the plane.
target_in_paper: Section 1 (Introduction), Problem 1: "Find the exact asymptotic value of D(n)," where D(P) is the number of distinct distances determined by pairs of points from a finite set P \subset \mathbb{R}^2 and D(n)=\min_{|P|=n} D(P).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s main planar Erdős distinct distances problem, uses the paper’s notation D(n), and correctly describes D(n) as the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set in the plane. It also matches the paper’s exact scope: unrestricted finite point sets in the Euclidean plane, with the goal of determining the asymptotic behavior of D(n).
missing_details: The paper first defines D(P) for a finite set P \subset \mathbb{R}^2 as the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points from P.
To make the question fully stand-alone, D(n) should be written explicitly as D(n)=\min\{D(P): P\subset \mathbb{R}^2, |P|=n\}.
It should be explicit that the distances are ordinary Euclidean distances in \mathbb{R}^2.
It should be explicit that the distances are taken over pairs of distinct points of the same set P.
It should specify that the asymptotic question is about the behavior as n\to\infty.
It helps to make clear that there are no additional restrictions on the point set (for example, no general-position, convexity, or lattice assumptions).
refined_question: Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points from a finite set P \subset \mathbb{R}^2, and let D(n)=\min\{D(P): P\subset \mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n\}. Determine the exact asymptotic value of D(n) as n\to\infty.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s headline open problem, not a neighboring variant. In Section 1, the paper defines D(P) and D(n) exactly in the planar Euclidean setting and then states Problem 1 as "Find the exact asymptotic value of D(n)." The surrounding introduction confirms that this is the unrestricted planar distinct distances problem originally posed by Erdős, with current context given by the upper bound D(n)=O(n/\sqrt{\log n}) and the Guth–Katz lower bound D(n)=\Omega(n/\log n). Because your draft already uses D(n), asks for exact asymptotic growth, and refers to n-point sets in the plane, it is already very close to the paper’s formulation; the only real improvements are to spell out D(P), the minimization over all P\subset\mathbb{R}^2 with |P|=n, and the Euclidean metric explicitly.

citations.label: Context: Erdős upper bound and Guth–Katz lower bound for D(n)
